# Python API reference

`import queuetruth as qt`. Every analysis function takes a spec (a Pydantic model from `qt.schemas` or a plain
dict, validated; unknown fields are an error) and returns the Pydantic summary model of the same JSON document the
CLI prints. Long operations release the GIL inside the extension. Tables are `pyarrow.Table`; where a table is an
input, any object implementing `__arrow_c_stream__` works (Polars, DuckDB results, pandas through pyarrow). Every
`QT-*` error raises `qt.QtError` (`.code`, `.message`, `.hint`); HTTP API errors raise `qt.QtApiError` (code
`QT-REMOTE-001`, `.problem`).

Names marked **SPEC 4.3** are the binding public API (SemVer applies to them). Other exported names are
listed because their modules export them, but they may change between minor versions. `queuetruth._core` is
internal.

Spec and summary models live in `queuetruth.schemas` and are documented field by field in [Schemas](schemas.md).

Package version: `0.3.0`.

`live import`: venue exports (`queuetruth.live.import_venue`), simulator reports (venues `sim_hftbacktest`, `sim_nautilus`, `sim_freqtrade`, `sim_hummingbot`, `sim_backtrader`, `sim_vectorbt`, `sim_lean`, `sim_backtesting_py`: `queuetruth.live.import_sim`, log venue `sim:<name>`, for `score --sim-log`) or a trading bot's live run (`freqtrade`, `hummingbot`: `queuetruth.live.import_bot`). `tz` (default: the spec's `tz`) is the account time zone of venue-local times (IBKR Flex). `options` go to the simulator or bot importer (`venue` = live venue of the instrument-map rows, `size_exp`, `key_from_client_id`, `order_key_map`; for bots `dry_run`, `log_tz`, `timeframe`, `pair_with`, ...; for backtesters `pair_with` = a canonical live-log directory, `timeframe`, `instrument`, ...); for a venue whose importer has options of its own (`ibkr_flex`: `flex_date_order`), those. Each importer's options are a typed model (`queuetruth.live.importers.by_venue(venue).options`); a wrong or unknown one fails `QT-CONFIG-001`. A venue registered by a plugin (`queuetruth.importers`) works the same.

### `HazardModel` **SPEC 4.3**

```python
class HazardModel(spec: HazardFitSpec | dict[str, Any]) -> None
```

Gradient-boosted hazard model with isotonic recalibration; `predict` returns `qt.hazard_predictions`.

| Method | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fit` | `(self, features: pa.Table, *, threads: int \| None = None) -> HazardModel` | Splits (purge / embargo), fits the GBDT on the train person-period rows and the isotonic layers on the calib split. Keeps the split table (`split_features`) and assignment (`split_result`) for scoring. `threads` (execution only) fixes the GBDT's OpenMP threads (`fit_threads`). A fit that raises leaves the model unfitted (no estimator, no split table, no cached hazards from an earlier fit). |
| `hazards` | `(self, x: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]` | Raw per-interval hazards `(h_fill, h_cancel)`, shape (rows, J), for a feature matrix in model order. |
| `load` | `(path: str, *, sha256: str \| None = None, trusted: bool = False, allow_pickle: bool = False) -> HazardModel` | Loads a saved model. `path` is the output directory or a file in it (`model.json`, `model.npz`). |
| `matrix` | `(self, features: pa.Table) -> np.ndarray` | The model's feature matrix of a features table (QT-INPUT-002 if a feature column is missing). |
| `predict` | `(self, features: pa.Table) -> pa.Table` | `qt.hazard_predictions`: one row per input row and grid horizon (input order, then horizon). `split` is taken from the input's `split` column when present, else `test`; `y_fill` / `censored` need `event_ns` and `cause` (else null / false). |
| `predict_arrays` | `(self, features: pa.Table) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]` | `h_fill`, `h_cancel`, `cif_fill_raw`, `cif_fill`, `cif_cancel`, `survival`, each (rows, J). |
| `predict_split` | `(self) -> pa.Table` | `predict(split_features)` through the hazard cache of `fit` (`split_arrays`: only rows not yet predicted are predicted). In-process only (`QT-USAGE-001` for a model that was loaded, not fitted here). |
| `save` | `(self, out_dir: str) -> None` | Writes `model.npz` and records its sha256 in the model card (`model.json`, written or updated). |
| `split_arrays` | `(self, mask: np.ndarray \| None = None) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]` | `predict_arrays(split_features)` (only the rows where the boolean `mask` is true when given), each row predicted at most once per fit and cached; equal to predicting those rows again. In-process only: a model that was loaded, not fitted here, has no split table (`QT-USAGE-001`). |
| `state` | `(self) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, np.ndarray]]` | `(meta, arrays)` of `model.npz` (`queuetruth.model.persist`). `fitted_with` is the version that fitted the model (kept through load, migrate and re-save), not the one saving it. |

### `Session` **SPEC 4.3**

```python
class Session(dataset: str, venue: str | None = None) -> None
```

Interactive replay session: `.advance_to(ts)`, `.bbo(inst)`, `.depth(inst, n)`, `.queue_ahead(...)`.

| Method | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `advance_events_to` | `(self, ts: int) -> None` | Replays whole events up to `ts`: in each partition, the complete events (runs ending with `F_LAST`) whose records are all at or before `ts`, read in feed order up to the first record past it; the records of an event not complete by then wait for a later call. When the data ends with every remaining record at or before `ts`, an unterminated tail is applied and ended as the end of a `replay` ends it (orders are still taken until `finish`). This is the cut of the agent sandbox's tape, so the state after a call is that of a `replay` of exactly that prefix (GIL released). `position` becomes `ts`; the held records of an incomplete event are applied first by the next `advance_to`, whatever its time. |
| `advance_to` | `(self, ts: int) -> None` | Replays every record with `ts_event <= ts` (GIL released). |
| `amend` | `(self, shadow_id: str, ts: int, new_qty: int) -> None` | Sends a priority-keeping reduction to `new_qty` at `ts` (at or after `position`). |
| `bbo` | `(self, instrument_id: int) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int, int] \| None] \| None` | Best bid and ask. |
| `cancel` | `(self, shadow_id: str, ts: int) -> None` | Sends a cancel at `ts` (at or after `position`); it takes effect after the cancel latency. |
| `depth` | `(self, instrument_id: int, n: int) -> tuple[list[tuple[int, int, int]], list[tuple[int, int, int]]]` | Top `n` levels per side. |
| `finish` | `(self) -> None` | Replays to the end of the data; the shadows still open end as at the end of a `replay`. |
| `queue_ahead` | `(self, instrument_id: int, side: str, price: int) -> tuple[int, int] \| None` | Displayed quantity and order count at a price. |
| `shadow_states` | `(self, shadow_ids: list[str]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]` | Each shadow as a `replay` ending now would report it, one dict per id: `status` (`pending`, `live` or `done`); the `qt.shadow_results` columns its state determines (`price` as resolved, `ts_live`, `ts_activated_event`, `ts_cancel_effective`, `ts_first_fill`, `ts_last_fill`, `ts_full_fill`, `filled_qty`, `n_fills`, `out_of_session`, ...) with `end_state` None until it is done; `ts_end`, when it ended; and `queue_ahead` / `rank` after the last processed event once it went live (the values a `queue_trajectory` row would show; sessions keep no trajectory). |
| `submit` | `(self, shadows: Any) -> None` | Sends shadows, each with `ts_submit` at or after `position`: a `qt.shadow_spec` table (any Arrow stream) or a list of row dicts (`shadow_id`, `instrument_id`, `side` `"B"` or `"A"`, `qty`, `ts_submit` in ns, and `price` for an absolute price or `offset_ticks` for a touch-relative one; optional `latency_ns`, `group`, `order_key`). All or none: when any row is refused (a duplicate id, a `ts_submit` before `position`, an instrument the dataset has no data for), none of them is sent. A row of a known instrument that no partition covers (a time outside its days) is taken and ends `censored_gap` at its `ts_live` without being replayed, as in `replay`. A cancel or amend is sent later with `cancel` / `amend`. |
| `take_fills` | `(self) -> pa.Table` | Shadow fills since the last call (`qt.shadow_fills`); if building the table fails, they stay for the next. |
| `take_results` | `(self) -> pa.Table` | Results of the shadows that ended since the last call (`qt.shadow_results`). |
| `with_orders` | `(spec: s.ReplaySpec \| dict[str, Any]) -> Session` | A session that also takes shadow orders while it runs. Every partition replays as `replay` would replay it with this spec (latency model and seed, fill rule, hidden-print policy, exclusions, the dataset's feed gaps and trading halts); `shadows` and `amends` stay unset, orders come from `submit`, `cancel` and `amend`, each at or after `position`. The session reads the data once however many orders it takes, and its fills and results equal those of one `replay` with every order in its input. |

## `queuetruth.integrity`

Integrity primitives, one implementation each (contracts layer): canonical JSON in its published byte forms, sha256 of bytes, text, files and streams, the hash-chain digests and the atlas Merkle tree.

| Name | Kind | Binding | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `canonical_bytes` | function |  | `(value: Any, form: Form = jcs) -> bytes` | `canonical_json(value, form)` as UTF-8. |
| `canonical_json` | function |  | `(value: Any, form: Form = jcs) -> str` | The canonical JSON text of `value` in `form` (module docstring). |
| `canonical_sha256` | function |  | `(value: Any, form: Form = jcs) -> str` | Hex sha256 of the canonical JSON of `value` in `form` (`queuetruth.integrity.canonical`). |
| `entry_digest` | function |  | `(entry: dict[str, Any], without: str) -> str` | Hex sha256 of the `jcs` canonical JSON of `entry` without its own hash field `without`. |
| `escape_string` | function |  | `(s: str) -> str` | A JSON string literal escaped as RFC 8785 says (the reference rule; `jcs` uses the equal C encoder). |
| `format_float` | function |  | `(x: float) -> str` | ECMAScript Number::toString of a finite float (shortest round-trip digits), as RFC 8785 writes numbers. |
| `leaf_hash` | function |  | `(leaf_doc: dict[str, Any]) -> str` | Hex leaf hash of one unit's leaf document. |
| `ledger_line` | function |  | `(record: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[bytes, str]` | (line with newline, hash) of a run ledger record: the canonical JSON of `{"hash": H, "record": R}` where `H` is the sha256 of the exact bytes of `R` in the line. |
| `merkle_proof` | function |  | `(leaves: Sequence[str], index: int) -> list[list[str]]` | Sibling path of leaf `index`: `[["L" or "R", sibling hex], ...]` from the leaf up (carried nodes skipped). |
| `merkle_root` | function |  | `(leaves: Sequence[str]) -> str` | Hex root over hex leaves, in the order given. |
| `sha256_bytes` | function |  | `(data: bytes) -> str` | Hex sha256 of `data`. |
| `sha256_file` | function |  | `(path: str \| Path, chunk: int = 1048576) -> str` | Hex sha256 of a file's bytes. |
| `sha256_stream` | function |  | `(stream: BinaryIO, chunk: int = 1048576) -> str` | Hex sha256 of everything left in a binary stream. |
| `sha256_text` | function |  | `(text: str) -> str` | Hex sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes of `text`. |
| `utf16_key` | function |  | `(s: str) -> bytes` | Sort key of an object member name under RFC 8785 (UTF-16 code units). |
| `value_text` | function |  | `(value: Any) -> str` | A value as text inside a rendered claim: strings verbatim, everything else `jcs` canonical JSON. |
| `verify_proof` | function |  | `(leaf: str, proof: Sequence[Sequence[str]], root: str) -> bool` | True when `proof` takes `leaf` to `root`. |

Constants: `CHUNK`, `FORMS`, `GENESIS_ZERO`.

## `queuetruth.units`

Human units at every boundary (plan section 3, principle 7): durations, horizons, prices, times and sides.

| Name | Kind | Binding | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DurationError` | class |  | | A duration or horizon that does not parse. `hint` says what to write instead. |
| `format_duration` | function |  | `(ns: Any, *, sig: int \| None = None, signed: bool = False) -> str` | A duration for people: `1_000_000_000` -> `"1s"`, `1_500_000_000` -> `"1.5s"`, `60_000_000_000` -> `"1min"`, `250_000_000` -> `"250ms"`, `0` -> `"0s"`. |
| `format_price` | function |  | `(ticks: Any, price_exp: int \| None, tick_size: Any = None) -> str` | A price for people: `150.12` (at least as many decimals as the tick size has, so `150.10` shows as `150.10` with a 0.01 tick; never rounded). An unknown scale prints the raw integer with its unit (`1501200 (price units, scale unknown)`); `None` is `"-"`. |
| `format_scaled` | function |  | `(v: Any, exp: int \| None) -> str` | A fixed-point integer `v * 10**exp` (a size, a quantity) as a decimal string without an exponent, trailing zeros trimmed (`1500, -3` -> `1.5`); with `exp` None or 0 the value as it is; `None` is `"-"`. |
| `horizon_key` | function |  | `(h: Any) -> str` | The key of a horizon in the JSON documents (decimal nanoseconds): `"1s"`, `1_000_000_000` and `"1000000000"` -> `"1000000000"`. `DurationError` when `h` is not a duration. |
| `horizon_label` | function |  | `(h: Any) -> str` | The human key of a horizon: `"1000000000"` -> `"1s"`, `60_000_000_000` -> `"1min"`. |
| `horizon_words` | function |  | `(h: Any) -> str` | A horizon in words, in the largest unit that holds it whole: `"1min"` -> `"1 minute"`, `10_000_000_000` -> `"10 seconds"`, `"1.5s"` -> `"1500 milliseconds"`. |
| `HorizonDict` | class |  | | A `{horizon: value}` map whose keys stay the JSON form (decimal nanoseconds, so it serialises and compares exactly as before) and that also answers human keys: `m["1s"]`, `m[1_000_000_000]` and `m["1000000000"]` are the same entry. `labels()` is a copy keyed `"1s"`. |
| `humanize_note` | function |  | `(text: str, tz: str \| None = None) -> str` | A warning or note written with raw integers (as stored in a summary's `warnings`) in human units, for display only: an epoch-nanosecond time after `ts`, `at`, `from`, `until` or `to` becomes local time with the zone named; a `<horizon_ns>=<better\|tie\|worse\|mixed\|n/a>` pair gets its horizon as `1s`. Anything else is unchanged. |
| `instrument_units` | function |  | `(dataset: Any, instrument_id: int, ts_ns: int \| None = None) -> dict[str, Any]` | `symbol`, `price_exp`, `size_exp`, `tick_size` and `session_tz` of an instrument on the session that holds `ts_ns` (else the instrument's first row); `{}` when the table or the instrument is missing. The values that turn its integers into human units. |
| `local_datetime` | function |  | `(ts_ns: Any, tz: str \| None) -> dt.datetime` | An epoch-nanosecond timestamp as an aware `datetime` in zone `tz` (UTC when `tz` is unknown), to the microsecond. |
| `local_time` | function |  | `(ts_ns: Any, tz: str \| None, *, digits: int = 6, date: bool = True, named: bool = True) -> str` | An epoch-nanosecond timestamp as venue-local wall time with the zone named: `2026-03-02 09:30:00.000123 America/New_York`. `digits` fraction digits (0 to 9, truncated); `date=False` leaves out the date; `named=False` leaves out the zone (for a table whose header names it, `zone_name(tz)`). An unknown or missing zone is written in UTC and says so; `None` is `"-"`. |
| `parse_duration` | function |  | `(value: Any, *, what: str = duration, bare_ns: bool = True) -> int` | Nanoseconds of a duration: `"1s"`, `"250ms"`, `"1min"`, `"1m"`, `"60 s"`, `"1.5s"`, `"100us"`, an `int` count of nanoseconds or its string. Case and surrounding spaces are ignored. Negative values, fractions of a nanosecond and values beyond the int64 range are `DurationError`. With `bare_ns=False` a string without a unit (other than `"0"`) is refused, for flags where `"5"` would be ambiguous. |
| `price_from_ticks` | function |  | `(ticks: Any, price_exp: int) -> Decimal` | The exact decimal price of a fixed-point integer price: `ticks * 10**price_exp` (`1_501_200, -4` -> `Decimal("150.12")`). |
| `side_word` | function |  | `(side: Any) -> str` | `buy` or `sell` for a side code (`B` / `A`, `bid` / `ask`, `1` / `-1`, `BUY` / `SELL`); any other value is returned as text, unchanged, and `None` is `"-"`. |
| `zone` | function |  | `(tz: str \| None) -> dt.tzinfo \| None` | The `tzinfo` of an IANA zone name (`UTC` for `"UTC"`), or None when the name is unknown or empty. |
| `zone_name` | function |  | `(tz: str \| None) -> str` | The name `local_time` writes for zone `tz`: the IANA name, or `UTC` when it is UTC, unknown or missing. |

Constants: `I64_MAX`, `UNITS`.

## `queuetruth.data`

`queuetruth data`: bring order-level data in, in one command.

| Name | Kind | Binding | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `add` | function |  | `(files: str \| Path \| Sequence[str \| Path], out: str \| Path, *, format: str \| None = None, venue: str \| None = None, date: str \| None = None, symbols: Sequence[str] \| None = None, attribution: list[dict[str, Any]] \| None = None, say: Say \| None = None) -> DataResult` | Ingests `files` into the dataset `out` (module docstring). An existing dataset at `out` keeps its days and gains the new ones (a day it already holds is `QT-INPUT-002`). `format`, `venue` and `date` override what is inferred (`date` is YYYY-MM-DD; for formats whose records carry dates it puts every record in that session); `symbols` keeps only those symbols; `attribution` entries are recorded in the dataset manifest. |
| `DataResult` | class |  | | The answer of `data add` / `data fetch iex`: `summary` is the one-line answer, `doc` the full document, `rows` one row per session date and symbol in human units. |
| `detect` | function |  | `(path: str \| Path, *, format: str \| None = None, venue: str \| None = None, date: str \| None = None) -> Detected` | What `path` is (module docstring). Given values win; `QT-USAGE-001` names what could not be inferred and why; `QT-INPUT-001` for a missing path. |
| `Detected` | class |  | | One input: what it is and how that was decided (`how`: format, venue and date, each in plain words). |
| `fetch_iex` | function |  | `(date: str \| dt.date, symbols: Sequence[str] \| str, out: str \| Path \| None = None, *, yes: bool = False, confirm: Callable[[FetchPlan], bool] \| None = None, progress: Progress \| None = None, say: Callable[[str], None] \| None = None, url: str \| None = None, min_free_bytes: int = 2147483648) -> DataResult` | Fetches one IEX DEEP+ day's `symbols` into the dataset `out` (default `iex-<date>`; an existing dataset gains the day). Downloads only with `yes` or when `confirm(plan)` returns True, else `QT-USAGE-001`. `url` streams another location (a mirror, or a local test server) instead of IEX's bucket. |
| `FetchPlan` | class |  | | What `fetch_iex` would do (no I/O): the day, symbols, URL and output dataset. |
| `plan_fetch` | function |  | `(date: str \| dt.date, symbols: Sequence[str] \| str, out: str \| Path \| None = None, *, url: str \| None = None) -> FetchPlan` | The plan of a fetch (module docstring); `QT-USAGE-001` for a bad date or symbol, or a day in the future. |

## `queuetruth.dataset`

One way to open, read, check and write a queuetruth dataset (plan section 5.3 step 3).

| Name | Kind | Binding | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `check_rel_path` | function |  | `(rel: str, where: str) -> Path` | `rel` as a relative path made only of normal components, else `QT-INPUT-002` (a manifest must not make a reader open `/etc/passwd` or a sibling dataset). The check is lexical and mirrors the engine's (`qt_ingest` `check_rel_path`): no absolute path, drive, `..`, leading `.` or NUL. Symlinks are followed, as the engine follows them (datasets with partitions on another volume are linked in). |
| `check_table_schema` | function |  | `(table: pa.Table \| pa.Schema, want: str, where: str \| Path) -> None` | `QT-INPUT-002` when the table carries a `qt.schema` other than `want` (a table without one is accepted: CSV files and tables written by other tools carry none). |
| `Dataset` | class |  | | An opened dataset directory or live log. Open one with `open_dataset`. |
| `dataset_id` | function |  | `(partition_shas: list[str], source_format: str) -> str` | SPEC 3.10 `dataset_id`: sha256 of the sorted partition-file sha256 list, newline-joined, then a newline and `source_format` (the rule of `qt_schema::json::dataset_id`). |
| `DatasetKind` | class |  | | What a directory holds. |
| `DatasetWriter` | class |  | | Writes the files of a dataset directory, records each file's `Files` entry (`name`, `rows`, `bytes`, `sha256`) and finally the manifest, atomically (`finalize`: a temporary name, then a rename), so a directory with a manifest is always complete. |
| `date_str` | function |  | `(days: int) -> str` | `YYYY-MM-DD` of a day number (days since 1970-01-01). |
| `day_number` | function |  | `(value: Any) -> int` | Days since 1970-01-01 of a `datetime.date`, a `YYYY-MM-DD` string or a day number. |
| `expansion_limit` | function |  | `(size: int, slack: int = 67108864) -> int` | Largest decoded size accepted for an input of `size` bytes on disk. |
| `Instrument` | class |  | | An instrument's identity and units on one session date. Prices are integers scaled by `10**price_exp`, sizes by `10**size_exp`; `tick_size` is in price units. |
| `instrument_rows` | function |  | `(t: pa.Table, where: str \| Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]` | Rows of a `qt.instruments` table with the known columns cast to their types and `session_date` as a day number (`QT-INPUT-002` naming the column when a value does not fit). |
| `json_text` | function |  | `(doc: Any, *, indent: int \| None = 2, ensure_ascii: bool = True, sort_keys: bool = False, allow_nan: bool = False) -> str` | The text a writer stores for a JSON document (a dict or a Pydantic model): `json.dumps` with these options and a trailing newline (NaN and Infinity refused unless `allow_nan`). |
| `Manifest` | class |  | | A manifest document as read (a read-only mapping in file order), with typed views of the fields readers use. |
| `open_dataset` | function |  | `(path: str \| Path, *, missing_ok: bool = False, contain: Contain \| None = None, bounded: bool = False, max_manifest_bytes: int \| None = None) -> Dataset` | Opens a queuetruth dataset directory (an MBO or L2 dataset, a prediction-market dataset) or a live or simulator log, and checks its manifest. |
| `Partition` | class |  | | One (instrument, session date) partition of a dataset manifest. |
| `PartitionFile` | class |  | | One Parquet file of a partition (path relative to the dataset root). |
| `read_manifest` | function |  | `(path: str \| Path, *, missing_ok: bool = True) -> dict[str, Any]` | The `manifest.json` of a directory as a dict (`{}` when absent and `missing_ok`); `QT-INPUT-002` when it does not parse. |
| `read_manifest_doc` | function |  | `(root: str \| Path, *, missing_ok: bool = False, contain: Callable[[Path], Path] \| None = None, max_bytes: int \| None = None) -> dict[str, Any] \| None` | The `manifest.json` of a directory as a dict; None when it is absent and `missing_ok`. `QT-INPUT-001` when absent, `QT-INPUT-002` when it is not a JSON object (NaN and Infinity are refused). |
| `read_parquet_bounded` | function |  | `(path: Path, *, columns: list[str] \| None = None, code: str = QT-INPUT-002, what: str = unreadable, slack: int = 67108864) -> pa.Table` | The Parquet file's table (only `columns` that exist when given), its decoded size bounded by `expansion_limit(file size, slack)`. `code` for a damaged file (any Arrow error, invalid UTF-8 in a column name), `QT-INPUT-002` for a file that decodes past the limit or has a nested column. |
| `Session` | class | SPEC 4.3 | | One instrument-day: the instrument's units that day and the session times. `midnight_utc_ns` is the local midnight in UTC ns; `open_s` and `close_s` are seconds after it (continuous trading). |
| `table_schema_name` | function |  | `(table: pa.Table \| pa.Schema) -> str \| None` | The `qt.schema` metadata of a table or schema, if any. |
| `TableDef` | class |  | | A logical table of a dataset: its `qt.schema` name and where its files are. |
| `Verification` | class |  | | What `Dataset.verify` found: `problems` is empty when every file the manifest lists is there with the sha256, size and row count it records. |
| `write_text_atomic` | function |  | `(path: Path, text: str) -> None` | Writes `text` to `path` through a temporary name in the same directory and a rename, so a reader sees the old file or the new one, never a part. |

Constants: `DATA_QUALITY_FILE`, `DATASET_SCHEMA`, `EVENTS_FILE`, `INSTRUMENT_TYPES`, `INSTRUMENTS_FILE`, `LIVE_SCHEMA`, `MANIFEST_FILE`, `MAX_RATIO`, `ORDERS_FILE`, `PREDICTION_MARKET_VENUES`, `PRICE_EXP_MAX`, `PRICE_EXP_MIN`, `SIM_PREFIX`, `SLACK`, `TABLES`.

## `queuetruth.stats`

Statistics used by evaluation and the scorer (SPEC 4.3 `queuetruth.stats`, 5.5.7, 5.6, 5.7.5).

| Name | Kind | Binding | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aalen_johansen` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(time: np.ndarray, cause: np.ndarray, causes: tuple[int, ...] = (1, 2)) -> dict[int, StepFunction]` | Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence per cause (cause 0 = censored). |
| `adjust` | function |  | `(p: np.ndarray, method: str, q: float = 0.05) -> np.ndarray` | Adjusted p-values for `method` in {none, holm, bh, by} (the `adj_method` values of `qt.score_tests`). |
| `auc_at` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(time: np.ndarray, event: np.ndarray, risk: np.ndarray, tau: float, censor: np.ndarray \| None = None) -> float` | Time-dependent cumulative/dynamic AUC at `tau` (improper; discrimination only). |
| `benjamini_hochberg` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(p: np.ndarray, q: float = 0.05) -> np.ndarray` | BH-adjusted p-values. |
| `benjamini_yekutieli` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(p: np.ndarray, q: float = 0.05) -> np.ndarray` | BY-adjusted p-values (BH times `sum_{i <= m} 1/i`). |
| `binom_exact_two_sided` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(k: int, n: int, p: float = 0.5) -> float` | Exact two-sided binomial p-value; for `p = 0.5`: `min(1, 2 * P(X <= min(k, n - k)))`, else scipy's binomtest. |
| `bins` | function |  | `(p: np.ndarray, n_bins: int = 10) -> np.ndarray` | Bin label per forecast (equal-count by stable rank; ties share the lowest bin of their group). |
| `block_counts` | function |  | `(n_blocks: int, b: int, seed: int) -> np.ndarray` | `(b, n_blocks)` multiplicity of each block in each replicate (same draws as `day_block_bootstrap`). |
| `block_counts_chunks` | function |  | `(n_blocks: int, b: int, seed: int, max_cells: int = 4000000) -> Iterator[np.ndarray]` | `(rows, n_blocks)` float multiplicity blocks whose concatenation equals `queuetruth.stats.block_counts(n_blocks, b, seed)`, each at most `max_cells` cells. |
| `block_labels` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(session_date: np.ndarray, ts_ns: np.ndarray, min_dates: int = 5) -> tuple[np.ndarray, str]` | Block label per row and the block kind: `("day", days since epoch)` with >= `min_dates` distinct dates, else `("30min", floor(ts / 30 min))` (UTC half-hours; equal to local half-hours for whole/half-hour UTC offsets). |
| `block_replicates` | function |  | `(blocks: np.ndarray, stat: Callable[[np.ndarray], float], b: int, seed: int) -> tuple[float, np.ndarray]` | `(stat(all rows), replicates)`; `stat` receives row indices (with repetition) into the caller's data. |
| `bootstrap_indices` | function |  | `(n: int, b: int, *, block_size: int \| None = None, kind: Bootstrap = stationary, seed: int = 0, test_id: str = selection) -> np.ndarray` | `b x n` row indices of a stationary, circular or moving block bootstrap (module docstring), drawn from `bootstrap_rng(seed, test_id)` in chunks of at most `CHUNK_ELEMENTS` indices (the tests use the same draws internally without materialising all `b x n` of them). |
| `bootstrap_p_two_sided` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(replicates: np.ndarray, null: float = 0.0) -> float` | `min(1, 2 min((1 + #{rep <= null}) / (1 + B), (1 + #{rep >= null}) / (1 + B)))` over the B finite replicates (SPEC 5.7.5 test, capped at 1 and never exactly 0 by the (1 + #) / (1 + B) form). |
| `bootstrap_rng` | function |  | `(seed: int, test_id: str) -> np.random.Generator` | `numpy.random.default_rng(stable_seed(seed, [b"bootstrap", test_id]))`. |
| `bootstrap_se` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(replicates: np.ndarray) -> float` | Bootstrap standard deviation (ddof = 1) of the finite replicates. |
| `bootstrap_seed` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(seed: int, test_id: str) -> int` | `stable_seed(seed, [b"bootstrap", test_id])`. |
| `brier` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(p: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> float` | Brier score. |
| `calibration_slope_intercept` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(p: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, eps: float = 1e-06) -> tuple[float, float]` | Logistic recalibration `(slope, intercept)` of `y` on `logit(clip(p, eps, 1 - eps))`. |
| `CI` | class |  | | Point estimate with a percentile confidence interval. |
| `ci_blocks` | function |  | `(session_date: np.ndarray, ts_ns: np.ndarray, instrument_id: np.ndarray, block: str = auto, *, labeler: Callable[[np.ndarray, np.ndarray], tuple[np.ndarray, str]] \| None = None, min_blocks: int = 5) -> CiBlocks` | Bootstrap blocks for one row per shadow (or order). `auto` keeps `block_labels` (day blocks with >= 5 dates, else 30-minute buckets) whenever that gives at least `MIN_CI_BLOCKS` blocks, so long runs are unchanged; on shorter data it uses (instrument, minute of `ts_ns`) clusters, the demo's choice, and when those are still fewer than `MIN_CI_BLOCKS` the result is not `available`. A forced kind is used as it is (minutes and half-hours are UTC buckets of `ts_ns`). `labeler` replaces `block_labels` for `auto` and `min_blocks` the threshold (tests). |
| `CiBlocks` | class |  | | Bootstrap blocks of a run: `labels` = dense block index per row (0..n-1), `kind` = `day`, `30min`, `1min` or `instrument_minute`, `n` = number of blocks, `requested` = the choice asked for. `available` is false with fewer than `MIN_CI_BLOCKS` blocks: callers then report no interval and no significance. |
| `clopper_pearson` | function |  | `(k: int, n: int, level: float = 0.95) -> tuple[float \| None, float \| None]` | Exact binomial interval for `k` successes in `n` (rows treated as independent). |
| `clustered_mcnemar` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(live_filled: np.ndarray, sim_filled: np.ndarray, clusters: np.ndarray, *, b: int = 1000, seed: int = 0, alpha: float = 0.05) -> ClusteredDiscordance` | Primary cluster-robust discordance test of paired fill outcomes (see module docstring). |
| `ClusteredDiscordance` | class |  | | Cluster-robust discordance test result (primary) with plain McNemar as secondary. |
| `day_block_bootstrap` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(blocks: np.ndarray, stat: Callable[[np.ndarray], float], b: int, seed: int, alpha: float = 0.05) -> CI` | Block bootstrap percentile CI over resampled blocks. |
| `deflated_sharpe_ratio` | function |  | `(sr: float, n: int, *, n_trials: int, var_sr: float, skew: float = 0.0, kurtosis: float = 3.0, mean_sr: float = 0.0) -> float` | PSR of the selected trial against `expected_max_sharpe(n_trials, var_sr, mean_sr)` (Bailey and Lopez de Prado 2014). Equal to PSR(0) for one trial with `mean_sr = 0`. |
| `dsr_from_returns` | function |  | `(returns: np.ndarray, trial_sharpes: np.ndarray, *, n_trials: int \| None = None) -> float` | DSR of `returns` (the selected trial) with `V = var(trial_sharpes, ddof = 1)` and `N = n_trials`, or `len(trial_sharpes)` without it; `trial_sharpes` holds the per-period Sharpes of every trial that has a series, the selected one included. Pass `n_trials` (>= `len(trial_sharpes)`) when trials without a series were also tried, as a trial ledger counts them, so the deflation is not understated. |
| `expected_max_sharpe` | function |  | `(n_trials: int, var_sr: float, mean_sr: float = 0.0) -> float` | Expected maximum Sharpe of `n_trials` independent skill-less trials whose Sharpes have variance `var_sr`. |
| `gray_test` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(time: np.ndarray, cause: np.ndarray, group: np.ndarray, cause_of_interest: int = 1) -> TestResult` | Gray's K-sample test on cumulative incidence (Gray 1988, rho = 0). |
| `holm` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(p: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray` | Holm-adjusted p-values. |
| `hosmer_lemeshow` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(p: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, n_bins: int = 10) -> TestResult` | Hosmer-Lemeshow test on the equal-count bins, `max(n_bins - 2, 1)` df. |
| `kaplan_meier` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(time: np.ndarray, event: np.ndarray) -> StepFunction` | Kaplan-Meier survival (event: bool). |
| `log_loss` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(p: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, eps: float = 1e-06) -> float` | Log loss with clipping. |
| `logrank` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(time_a: np.ndarray, event_a: np.ndarray, time_b: np.ndarray, event_b: np.ndarray) -> TestResult` | Two-sample log-rank test (matches lifelines `logrank_test`). |
| `mcnemar` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(b: int, c: int) -> McNemarResult` | McNemar test: chi2_cc, p_chi2, p_exact, odds_ratio, Wald CI on the log odds ratio. |
| `McNemarResult` | class |  | | McNemar test on discordant counts (SPEC 5.7.5). |
| `McsResult` | class |  | | Model confidence set: `included` = column indices (ascending) with `p_values > alpha`; `eliminated` = the elimination order (the surviving model last); `step_p` = the test p-value at each elimination; `studentize` = `"fixed"` (Hansen, Lunde and Nason) or `"wild"` (wild cluster bootstrap-t), module docstring. |
| `min_track_record_length` | function |  | `(sr: float, *, sr_benchmark: float = 0.0, skew: float = 0.0, kurtosis: float = 3.0, alpha: float = 0.05) -> float` | Track record length at which `PSR(sr_benchmark) = 1 - alpha` (inf when `sr <= sr_benchmark`). |
| `model_confidence_set` | function |  | `(losses: np.ndarray, *, alpha: float = 0.1, method: "Literal[R, max]" = R, b: int = 1000, seed: int = 0, test_id: str = mcs, bootstrap: Bootstrap = stationary, block_size: int \| None = None, blocks: np.ndarray \| None = None, indices: np.ndarray \| None = None, studentize: Studentize = auto) -> McsResult` | Hansen-Lunde-Nason MCS on an `n x m` loss matrix (rows = observations, columns = models). `studentize="auto"` is the wild cluster bootstrap-t (`"wild"`) with `blocks=` and the fixed bootstrap variance of Hansen, Lunde and Nason (`"fixed"`) otherwise (module docstring). |
| `murphy` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(p: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, n_bins: int = 10) -> dict[str, float]` | Murphy decomposition: brier, reliability, resolution, uncertainty, within_bin (they sum exactly to brier). |
| `obuchowski` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(b_k: np.ndarray, c_k: np.ndarray, n_k: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, float] \| None` | `(z, p)` of the Obuchowski cluster-adjusted McNemar test from per-cluster counts; None if undefined. |
| `paired_permutation` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(x_live: np.ndarray, x_sim: np.ndarray, stat: Callable[..., float], b: int, seed: int) -> TestResult` | Paired permutation test: `stat(x_live, x_sim)` vs `b` arm-swapped resamples (rows = orders). |
| `PboResult` | class |  | | CSCV outcome; arrays are per combination, in `itertools.combinations(range(S), S // 2)` order. |
| `percentile_ci` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(replicates: np.ndarray, alpha: float = 0.05) -> tuple[float, float]` | Percentile interval of the finite replicates (NaN if none). |
| `probabilistic_sharpe_ratio` | function |  | `(sr: float, n: int, *, skew: float = 0.0, kurtosis: float = 3.0, sr_benchmark: float = 0.0) -> float` | `Phi((SR - SR*) / sigma(SR))` (Bailey and Lopez de Prado 2012); an infinite `SR` (a constant non-zero series) reads 1 above the benchmark and 0 below. |
| `probability_of_backtest_overfitting` | function |  | `(performance: np.ndarray, *, n_splits: int = 16, metric: "Literal[sharpe, mean] \| Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray]" = sharpe) -> PboResult` | PBO by combinatorially symmetric cross-validation (module docstring). `performance` is `T x N` (periods x trials); `metric` maps a `t x N` row subset to `N` performances (callables get the rows in time order). |
| `psr_from_returns` | function |  | `(returns: np.ndarray, sr_benchmark: float = 0.0) -> float` | PSR of a return series with its own sample moments. |
| `ratio_replicates` | function |  | `(counts: np.ndarray, num: np.ndarray, den: np.ndarray, *, summation: "Literal[matmul, elementwise]" = matmul) -> np.ndarray` | Bootstrap replicates of `sum num / sum den` from per-block sums and block multiplicities `counts` (`(b, n_blocks)`); NaN where a replicate's denominator is not positive. |
| `reliability_table` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(p: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, n_bins: int = 10) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]` | Reliability table with Wilson CIs: columns bin, count, mean_p, observed_rate, p_min, p_max, rate_lo, rate_hi. |
| `sharpe_moments` | function |  | `(returns: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, int, float, float]` | `(SR, n, skewness, kurtosis)`: biased sample moments, Pearson (non-excess) kurtosis (3 for constant series). |
| `sharpe_ratio` | function |  | `(returns: np.ndarray) -> float` | Per-period Sharpe ratio `mean / std (ddof = 1)`; 0 for a constant zero series, `+-inf` for a constant non-zero one. |
| `sharpe_ratio_std` | function |  | `(sr: float, n: int, *, skew: float = 0.0, kurtosis: float = 3.0) -> float` | Standard error of the Sharpe estimator, `sqrt((1 - g3 SR + (g4 - 1) / 4 SR^2) / (n - 1))`. |
| `spa_test` | function |  | `(benchmark: np.ndarray, models: np.ndarray, *, b: int = 1000, seed: int = 0, test_id: str = spa, bootstrap: Bootstrap = stationary, block_size: int \| None = None, blocks: np.ndarray \| None = None, indices: np.ndarray \| None = None, studentize: bool = True) -> SpaResult` | Hansen's test of superior predictive ability on losses: H0 = no model beats the benchmark. |
| `SpaResult` | class |  | | Hansen's SPA test (module docstring). `mean_diff[k] = mean(L_benchmark - L_k)` (positive = model better), `omega[k]` the standard deviation of `sqrt(n) mean_diff[k]`, `t[k] = sqrt(n) mean_diff[k] / omega[k]`. |
| `spiegelhalter_z` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(p: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> TestResult` | Spiegelhalter z test (two-sided normal p-value). |
| `splitmix64` | function |  | `(x: int) -> int` | One splitmix64 step (adds the golden gamma, then mixes), as `qt_types::splitmix64`. |
| `stable_seed` | function |  | `(run_seed: int, parts: Sequence[bytes \| str]) -> int` | FNV-1a 64 over `run_seed` (8 LE bytes), then per part its length (4 LE bytes) and bytes; then splitmix64. |
| `StepFunction` | class |  | | Right-continuous step function: `value[i]` holds on `[time[i], time[i + 1])`; `time[0] = 0` for estimators. |
| `stepm` | function |  | `(benchmark: np.ndarray, models: np.ndarray, *, alpha: float = 0.05, b: int = 1000, seed: int = 0, test_id: str = stepm, bootstrap: Bootstrap = stationary, block_size: int \| None = None, blocks: np.ndarray \| None = None, indices: np.ndarray \| None = None, studentize: bool = True, recenter: Recenter = upper) -> StepMResult` | Stepwise multiple testing of every model against the benchmark at familywise error `alpha`. |
| `StepMResult` | class |  | | Romano-Wolf StepM: `superior` = models (column indices, ascending) whose `H_k: E[L_benchmark - L_k] <= 0` is rejected; `steps[j]` = the models rejected at step `j`, `critical_values[j]` its critical value (t units). |
| `TestResult` | class |  | | A test statistic and its p-value. |
| `tost_from_ci` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(ci90: tuple[float, float], margin: float) -> bool` | Equivalence iff the 90% CI lies inside `[-margin, margin]`. |
| `tost_p` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(estimate: float, se: float, margin: float) -> float` | TOST p-value `max(1 - Phi((est + m) / se), Phi((est - m) / se))`. |
| `tost_p_bootstrap` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(replicates: np.ndarray, margin: float) -> float` | TOST p-value from bootstrap replicates (SPEC 5.7.5, M22): `max(frac(rep <= -margin), frac(rep >= margin))` over the finite replicates; NaN when there is none or the margin is NaN. |
| `uno_c_index` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(time: np.ndarray, event: np.ndarray, risk: np.ndarray, tau: float \| None = None, censor: np.ndarray \| None = None) -> float` | Uno's concordance index (improper; discrimination only). |
| `wilcoxon_signed_rank` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(d: np.ndarray, zero_method: str = wilcox) -> WilcoxonResult` | Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, `scipy.stats.wilcoxon(d, zero_method, method="auto")`; NaN if no data. |
| `WilcoxonResult` | class |  | | Wilcoxon signed-rank result (matches `scipy.stats.wilcoxon`). |
| `wilson` | function |  | `(k: float, n: float, *, z: float = 1.959963984540054, edges: "Literal[exact, clip, none]" = exact) -> tuple[float, float] \| None` | Wilson score interval for `k` successes in `n` trials (module docstring for `edges`). |

## `queuetruth.model`

Learned L2 fill model: discrete-time competing-risk hazard (SPEC 4.3 `queuetruth.model`, 5.5).

| Name | Kind | Binding | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assemble_card` | function |  | `(model: HazardModel, *, model_id: str, scores: dict[str, Any] \| None, files: list[dict[str, Any]], warnings: list[str], zoo: dict[str, Any] \| None = None) -> HazardModelCard` | Builds and validates the `qt.hazard_model_card` document. |
| `auc_at` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(event_ns: np.ndarray, cause: np.ndarray, risk: np.ndarray, tau_ns: int, *, censoring: CensoringKM \| None = None) -> float \| None` | Cumulative/dynamic IPCW AUC of the fill cause at `tau` (improper): cases fill by `tau` (weight `1/G(e-)`), controls survivors (`1/G(tau-)`) and cancels by `tau` (`1/G(e-)`); ties count 1/2. None without both classes. Arguments follow `queuetruth.stats.auc_at(time, event, risk, tau, ...)` (times, outcome, risk, tau; SPEC 4.3). |
| `c_index_uno` | function |  | `(risk: np.ndarray, event_ns: np.ndarray, cause: np.ndarray, tau_ns: int, *, censoring: CensoringKM \| None = None, max_rows: int = 20000, seed: int = 0) -> float \| None` | Uno-type IPCW concordance of the fill cause truncated at `tau` (improper): for a fill `i` with `e_i <= tau` the comparable `j` are `e_j > e_i` or cancels with `e_j <= e_i`; pair weight `1/G(e_i-)^2`; concordant if `risk_i > risk_j` (ties 1/2). Above `max_rows` rows a seeded subsample of `max_rows` rows is used. |
| `censoring_km` | function |  | `(event_ns: np.ndarray, cause: np.ndarray) -> CensoringKM` | KM of the censoring distribution from `(event_ns, cause)`; `cause` as strings or codes (0 = censor). |
| `CensoringKM` | class |  | | Kaplan-Meier survival of censoring: `value[i] = G(times[i])` (right-continuous). |
| `cif_from_hazards` | function |  | `(h_fill: np.ndarray, h_cancel: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]` | `(CIF_fill, CIF_cancel, S)` per grid point from per-interval hazards (shape (n, J)), SPEC 5.5.4. |
| `Climatology` | class |  | | Fitted climatology: CIF_fill on the grid per fine stratum, per instrument x side, and overall. |
| `expand_person_period` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(features: pa.Table, grid_ns: list[int]) -> pa.Table` | Person-period rows (SPEC 5.5.3): every input column, then `row_id` (input row index), `interval_idx` (1..J), `log_tau_end` (ln of `tau_j` in s) and `target` (0 none, 1 fill, 2 cancel). |
| `fit_hazard` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(spec: HazardFitSpec \| dict[str, Any]) -> HazardModelCard` | `fit-hazard`: reads `qt.features`, fits, writes `predictions.parquet` (every split), `model.npz` and `model.json` under `out` (nothing is written when `out` is null) and returns the model card. |
| `HazardModel` | class | SPEC 4.3 | | Gradient-boosted hazard model with isotonic recalibration; `predict` returns `qt.hazard_predictions`. |
| `ibs` | function |  | `(brier_by_tau: list[float] \| np.ndarray, grid_ns: list[int]) -> float` | Integrated Brier `sum_j BS(tau_j) (tau_j - tau_{j-1}) / tau_J` (`tau_0 = 0`). |
| `ipcw_brier` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(cif_fill: np.ndarray, event_ns: np.ndarray, cause: np.ndarray, tau_ns: int, *, censoring: CensoringKM \| None = None) -> float` | IPCW Brier of the fill cause at `tau`: `mean_i w_i (1{e_i <= tau, fill} - F_fill(tau \| x_i))^2`. |
| `ipcw_logloss` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(cif_fill: np.ndarray, cif_cancel: np.ndarray, event_ns: np.ndarray, cause: np.ndarray, tau_ns: int, *, censoring: CensoringKM \| None = None) -> float` | IPCW competing-risk log loss at `tau` (Alberge et al. 2024 eq. 2), `S = max(1 - F_fill - F_cancel, 1e-12)`; `censoring` defaults to the KM of censoring of the same rows. |
| `LegacyPickleWarning` | class |  | | A legacy `model.pkl` was unpickled (`allow_pickle=True`): migrate it to `model.npz`. |
| `make_split` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(features: pa.Table, split: dict[str, Any] \| SplitSpec \| None = None, *, h_max_ns: int \| None = None, sessions: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] \| None = None) -> pa.Table` | Adds the `split` column and drops purged / embargoed rows (SPEC 5.5.6). `h_max_ns` defaults to `max(60 s, max event_ns)`; `sessions` maps `YYYY-MM-DD` to `(start_ns, end_ns)` session bounds. |
| `model_feature_names` | function |  | `(table: pa.Table \| pa.Schema, privileged: bool) -> list[str]` | Model inputs in table order: `side_sign`, then every non-fixed column; `p_*` columns only if `privileged`. |
| `model_sha256` | function |  | `(card: Any) -> str \| None` | The sha256 of the model file a `qt.hazard_model_card` lists (`model.npz`, else a legacy `model.pkl`; model or dict; None when neither is listed): the trusted digest to pass to `HazardModel.load` when the card comes from `fit_hazard` itself. |
| `rcll` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(h_fill: np.ndarray, h_cancel: np.ndarray, event_ns: np.ndarray, cause: np.ndarray, grid_ns: list[int]) -> float` | Right-censored log likelihood loss (mean `-ln P(observed)`, probabilities floored at 1e-12). |
| `split_assignment` | function |  | `(features: pa.Table, split: SplitSpec \| dict[str, Any] \| None = None, *, h_max_ns: int \| None = None, sessions: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] \| None = None) -> SplitResult` | Computes the split of every row (see the module docstring) without dropping anything. |
| `TreeEnsemble` | class |  | | Prediction form of a fitted `HistGradientBoostingClassifier` (module docstring). |

| `annotate` | function |  | `(cal: CalibrationResult) -> CalibrationResult` | A copy of `cal` with the structured `trust` field (schema 1.1) and its `warnings` ending with the `beats_default` and `verdict` lines (replacing older ones). The assessment is recomputed from the lines and the numbers: an earlier structured field (e.g. the Rust part's, which has no held-out comparison) is replaced. |
| `assess` | function |  | `(cal: CalibrationResult, fmt: Callable[[int], str] \| None = None) -> Trust` | Exportability of a calibration (see the module doc). The structured `trust` field (schema 1.1) decides when present: its `verdict` / `reasons` and `beats_default` labels win, with texts from the `trust:` lines or the recomputed reasons; without it the assessment is computed from the lines and the numbers. `fmt` writes the horizons in the reason texts (default `dur`, the form stored in the calibration's warnings; displays pass `queuetruth.units.format_duration`). |
| `export_snippets` | function |  | `(cal: CalibrationResult, latency_npz: str \| None = None) -> Exports` | The `exports` object of a calibration result (snippets + notes; `latency_npz` kept or set). |
| `ExportNote` | class |  | | A caveat that accompanies an exported snippet (hftbacktest #312/#316, conflated L2, omitted lines). Emitted by `run_export` so `queuetruth export hftbacktest\|nautilus` prints it on stderr (`warning: ...`) next to the text, which keeps the exact SPEC 5.10 layout. |
| `ExportRefused` | class |  | | `QT-CALIB-001`: the calibration is degenerate, at a grid edge or does not beat the default out of sample. Exit code 1 (the export completed its check and the check failed), like a failed gate. |
| `hftbacktest_notes` | function |  | `(cal: CalibrationResult) -> list[str]` | Notes accompanying `hftbacktest_snippet` (always includes #316/#312 and the conflated-L2 caveat). |
| `hftbacktest_replay_script` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(schedule: Any = None, *, amends: Any = None, live: str \| None = None, dataset: str \| None = None, units: Mapping[int, Units \| Mapping[str, Any]] \| None = None, post_only: Mapping[str, bool] \| bool \| None = None, entry: str = exchange_ack, step_ns: int = 10000000, window_ns: int = 300000000000, script_name: str = hbt_replay.py) -> str` | Standalone hftbacktest 2.4.4 replay script for a schedule (see the module doc). |
| `hftbacktest_snippet` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(cal: CalibrationResult, exchange: str \| None = None) -> str` | Paste-ready hftbacktest `BacktestAsset` chain (SPEC 5.10 layout plus the fit / held-out header lines). `exchange` is `no_partial` (default, runs on the released hftbacktest 2.4.4) or `partial` (hftbacktest #312). |
| `latency_rows` | function |  | `(live_dir: str \| Path) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]` | (structured array, number of submitted orders skipped; reasons in `latency_table`). |
| `latency_table` | function |  | `(live_dir: str \| Path) -> tuple[np.ndarray, dict[str, int]]` | (structured array, orders skipped per reason in `SKIP_REASONS`). |
| `LatencyRowsSkipped` | class |  | | Orders without a usable latency row (see the module doc). |
| `load_calibration` | function |  | `(path: str \| Path) -> CalibrationResult` | Reads a `qt.calibration_result` JSON file (`calibration.json` or `fit.json`, or a directory holding one). |
| `nautilus_notes` | function |  | `(cal: CalibrationResult) -> list[str]` | Notes accompanying `nautilus_snippet`. |
| `nautilus_replay_strategy` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(schedule: Any = None, *, amends: Any = None, live: str \| None = None, dataset: str \| None = None, units: Mapping[int, Units \| Mapping[str, Any]] \| None = None, post_only: Mapping[str, bool] \| bool \| None = None, entry: str = exchange_ack, instrument_ids: Mapping[int, str] \| None = None, nautilus_venue: str = SIM) -> str` | NautilusTrader strategy module text replaying a schedule (see the module doc). Instrument ids default to `<symbol>.<nautilus_venue>`. |
| `nautilus_snippet` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(cal: CalibrationResult) -> str` | NautilusTrader `FillModel` / `LatencyModel` lines for the fitted values only (SPEC 5.10 layout, D4). |
| `read_schedule` | function |  | `(schedule: Any, amends: Any = None) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]]]` | (leg rows, amend rows) of a `qt.shadow_spec` path / table / rows; amends default to the sibling `<stem>_amends.parquet` (`shadows from-live`) or `amends.parquet` / `schedule_amends.parquet` next to it. |
| `refusal` | function |  | `(cal: CalibrationResult, target: str) -> ExportRefused \| None` | The `ExportRefused` error of a non-exportable calibration (None when exportable). |
| `replay_schedule` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(target: Target, out: str \| Path, *, schedule: Any = None, amends: Any = None, live: str \| None = None, dataset: str \| None = None, units: Mapping[int, Units \| Mapping[str, Any]] \| None = None, post_only: Mapping[str, bool] \| bool \| None = None, entry: str = exchange_ack, step_ns: int = 10000000, window_ns: int = 300000000000, instrument_ids: Mapping[int, str] \| None = None, nautilus_venue: str = SIM) -> ReplayExport` | Writes the replay program for `target` to `out` (CLI request: `queuetruth export replay-schedule --target hftbacktest\|nautilus --schedule FILE [--live DIR] [--data DIR] --out FILE`). |
| `ReplayExport` | class |  | | Result of `replay_schedule`. |
| `run_export` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(spec: ExportSpec \| dict[str, Any], *, force: bool = False) -> ExportSummary` | Python export targets: `hftbacktest`/`nautilus` (text, optionally written to `out`) and `latency_npz`. |
| `write_latency_npz` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(live_dir: str, out: str) -> FileEntry` | IntpOrderLatency `.npz` from a live log (written to `npz_path(out)`); raises `QT-INPUT-002` when no order has the needed timestamps. Skipped orders are reported as a `LatencyRowsSkipped` warning. |
| `write_npz` | function |  | `(arr: np.ndarray, out: str \| Path, member: str = data) -> Path` | Deterministic `np.savez_compressed(out, data=arr)` equivalent. |

Constants: `LATENCY_DTYPE`.

## `queuetruth.report`

Static self-contained HTML report (SPEC 4.3 `queuetruth.report`, 5.9).

| Name | Kind | Binding | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `render` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(spec: ReportSpec \| dict[str, Any], *, leaderboard_sort_horizon_ns: int \| None = None) -> ReportSummary` | Renders the report of SPEC 5.9 to `spec.out` and returns its `qt.report_summary`. The zoo leaderboard is sorted by absolute fill-rate bias at the keyword `leaderboard_sort_horizon_ns`, else the spec field of that name, else 60 s. |

## `queuetruth.frames`

Run outputs as pandas or polars DataFrames, for notebooks and ad-hoc analysis.

| Name | Kind | Binding | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `available_backends` | function |  | `() -> list[str]` | The installed DataFrame libraries among `BACKENDS`, in `BACKENDS` order. |
| `held_out` | function |  | `(calibration: Any, backend: str \| None = None) -> Any` | Held-out metrics of a calibration as one row per arm, model and horizon (`qt.calibration_result`: a `CalibrationResult`, its dict, a calibration output directory or its `calibration.json`). |
| `leaderboard` | function |  | `(zoo: Any, backend: str \| None = None) -> Any` | The zoo leaderboard as one row per model and horizon (`qt.zoo_summary`: a `ZooSummary`, its dict, a zoo output directory or its `summary.json`). |
| `load_run` | function |  | `(path: str \| Path, backend: str \| None = None, verify: bool = False) -> RunFrames` | Opens a run output directory (or its summary JSON file) as a `RunFrames`. |
| `read` | function |  | `(path: str \| Path, expect: str \| None = None, columns: Sequence[str] \| None = None, backend: str \| None = None, filters: Any = None) -> Any` | Reads one queuetruth Parquet table as a DataFrame. |
| `records` | function |  | `(doc: Any, field: str, backend: str \| None = None, *, instruments: Any = None, human: bool = True) -> Any` | A list-of-objects field of any summary document as a DataFrame, one row per element. |
| `resolve_backend` | function |  | `(backend: str \| None = None) -> str` | The backend to use: `backend`, else env `QT_FRAMES_BACKEND`, else `"auto"` (pandas, then polars). |
| `RunFrames` | class |  | | One run output directory: its summary document and its Parquet tables as DataFrames. |
| `scorecards` | function |  | `(scores: Any, backend: str \| None = None) -> Any` | Scorecards side by side, one row each (`qt.scorecard_summary`). |
| `to_frame` | function |  | `(data: Any, backend: str \| None = None) -> Any` | One Arrow table (or record batch, or list of row dicts) as a pandas or polars DataFrame (module docstring). |

Constants: `BACKENDS`, `ENV_BACKEND`, `SUMMARY_FILES`.

## `queuetruth.client`

HTTP client for the queuetruth service (SPEC 4.5; env `QT_API_URL`, `QT_API_KEY`).

| Name | Kind | Binding | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Client` | class |  | | Client for every `/v1` endpoint (idempotency keys, problems -> `QtApiError`, job waiting, downloads). |
| `job_error` | function |  | `(job: m.Job) -> QtApiError` | `QtApiError` for a job that did not succeed (its problem, or a synthesized one). |
| `Jobs` | class |  | | `client.jobs`: list, get, cancel, submit, wait, files and verified downloads. |
| `new_idempotency_key` | function |  | `() -> str` | A fresh random idempotency key (1..255 chars, SPEC 8.6). |
| `problem_from_response` | function |  | `(response: httpx.Response) -> dict[str, Any]` | The `qt.problem` document of an error response (parsed or synthesized). |
| `problem_slug` | function |  | `(problem: dict[str, Any]) -> str \| None` | The problem's slug: its `code`, or the last path segment of a queuetruth `type` URL. |
| `ReportRecord` | class |  | | `GET /v1/reports/{id}`: `{id, job_id, files}`. |
| `RunRecord` | class |  | | `GET /v1/{replays\|calibrations\|scorecards}/{id}`: `{id, spec, job_id, summary?}` with a typed summary. |
| `Submission` | class |  | | Response of a job-creating POST (`{id, job}`), with `replayed` = the `Idempotent-Replayed` header. |

Constants: `DEFAULT_API_URL`, `ENV_API_KEY`, `ENV_API_URL`, `ESTIMATE_KINDS`, `RUN_KINDS`, `TERMINAL_JOB_STATES`.

## `queuetruth.runner`

One runner for every operation (plan section 5.3, step 8): `run(name, spec, out=..., context=...)`.

| Name | Kind | Binding | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `check_dataset_tree` | function |  | `(top: Path, inside: Callable[[Path], Path \| None], what: str, *, require_manifest: bool = True) -> None` | A dataset directory: `manifest.json` must exist when `require_manifest` (`QT-INPUT-001`; checked first, so a broad directory such as the root is refused without walking it), and no entry may be a symlink for which `inside` returns None (`QT-CONFIG-001`). At most `MAX_TREE_ENTRIES` entries are walked (`QT-INPUT-002` beyond). |
| `document_of` | function |  | `(result: Any, name: str) -> dict[str, Any]` | The JSON document of an operation's result: a Pydantic document, a result object with `.doc`, or a dict. |
| `produced_files` | function |  | `(out: Path \| None) -> list[Path]` | Every file at `out` (a file or a directory; symlinks are not followed), sorted. |
| `Roots` | class |  | | Allowed roots (real paths). Relative paths start at `base` (default: the first root). `env_hint` names the settings that set the roots, for the error hint. |
| `run` | function | SPEC 4.3 | `(name: str, spec: BaseModel \| dict[str, Any], *, out: str \| os.PathLike[str] \| None = None, context: RunContext \| None = None) -> RunOutcome` | Runs the operation `name` on `spec` (module docstring). `out` is a directory for the outputs; it replaces the spec's own output field (with the operation's `out_name` inside it, such as `shadows.parquet`). |
| `RunContext` | class |  | | Who runs the operation, and what it may touch (module docstring). |
| `RunOutcome` | class |  | | One run: the operation, its JSON `document`, the answer line (`summary`, when the result has one), the warnings it raised, the files it wrote (sorted) and its output location. |
| `summary_of` | function |  | `(result: Any) -> str \| None` | The answer line of a result (`.summary` of the shared result shape), if it has one. |

Constants: `DATASET_FIELDS`, `MAX_TREE_ENTRIES`.
